text:
maria: Quick sync — I ran an nsys + perfetto sweep on a 4xA100 multi-GPU run after the recent kernel-selection change. Posting raw-ish notes and a couple of snippets. Hoping for quick pointers before I dig deeper.

nsys command I used:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,nccl -o /tmp/profiles/multi4_run_1710609876 --sample=none --force-overwrite --capture-range=nvtx python -u run_inference.py --model redwood/ev-attn --pp 2 --tp 2 --batcher-config '{"max_latency_ms":5,"bucketing":"time"}'
```
Summary observations (from timeline + nsys stats + perfetto slices):
- NCCL all-reduce windows are largely serialized: collective op shows up staggered across ranks with ~60% idle gaps where ranks wait for a late peer. Total NCCL all-reduce time ~320ms but ~240ms spent in gap/wait.
- Compute kernels (fused_attention_long) are large (~7–9ms) and appear to block other streams; kernel launches sometimes don't overlap with NCCL on other ranks.
- KV cache behavior: frequent device->host async memcpy bursts between iterations. Looks like LRU eviction triggered by our shared allocator when batcher pushes larger buckets. Those memcpys align with spikes in host CPU work and correspond to stalls in the CUDA stream.
- Batching heuristic (time-based bucketing) results in high seq-len variance within the same batch; kernel selection chooses fallback/unfused kernels on ~30% of batches leading to big perf regression.

Snippet from `nsys stats` kernel timeline (abridged):
```
Kernel                          Calls   Total Time (ms)   Avg (ms)
fused_attention_long           512     4096              8.0
attention_unfused              234     936               4.0
ncclAllReduce_rank0            48      320               6.6
MemcpyAsync D2H                120     480               4.0
```
Perfetto flame: nccl regions never overlap compute on rank2; rank0 shows compute then long idle while waiting for nccl on rank1.

Questions / asks:
1) Are there known env flags to encourage NCCL overlap with compute (we currently use default NCCL settings)?
2) Any heuristics to quickly detect when KV cache evictions are causing host/device thrash? (I can capture allocator debug, but would prefer a quick pattern detection)
3) Is there a fast way to force the runtime to pick the fused kernel for profiling to see if that alone fixes the perf cliff?

cc @dan @alex @tyler : any quick ideas?

---
dan: quick thoughts — good catch. A few things to try that have helped us before:
- set `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` and `NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS` (helps avoid unexpected p2p fallbacks across PCI domains). Also try `NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE=PARALLEL` — it can allow async kernels to be scheduled more aggressively.
- check `NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME` so NVLINK/nic selection is stable across nodes. Misrouting can serialize coll ops.
- run a short `nv-nsight` capture or `nvprof` on a single rank with `--trace=cuda,nccl` to see per-kernel occupancy and whether the kernel is serialized at the driver level.

Also: if fused_attention_long is huge, try forcing smaller sequence lengths (pad/bucket) for a run to see if the kernel becomes two shorter kernels (helps determine if it's fusion logic).

---
alex: small repro hacks that are quick:
- to force the runtime to pick fused kernel: temporarily set `RT_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=fast-fused` (we have this internal switch in the dev build) or use the internal `--force-kernel=FUSED_ATTENTION` flag in the binary. If you don't have the dev build, add an NVTX tag before the kernel selection and grep logs for chosen kernel id.
- for KV cache: set `KV_CACHE_MAX_ITEMS` to a huge number on the test run to disable eviction. If memcpys disappear, you found the culprit. Also `ALLOCATOR_DEBUG=1` prints evictions to stderr which you can grep.
- quick metric: if Memcpy D2H time spikes correlate with higher host CPU %sys and a pause in CUDA queue length, that's a tell. Perfetto shows the memcopy slices nicely.

---
tyler: two experiments to run in parallel:
1) NCCL overlap check: run with `NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE=PARALLEL` + `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` + `NCCL_TOPO_DUMP_FILE=/tmp/nccl_topo.json`, capture `nsys` and grep for `enqueue` vs `start` differences. If enqueue happens earlier but start delayed, driver serialization.
2) KV & batching isolation: switch batcher to `bucketing: seq_length` (bucket size 8) and `pad_bucket_max_ratio=1.2` so batches are homogeneous. Also set `KV_CACHE_MAX_ITEMS=1e9` to disable eviction. Compare end-to-end p50/p95 and kernel selection counts.

If both changes fix different pieces, we can split the rollout: batching heuristic change + a follow-up NVLINK/NCCL tuning.

---
ci-bot: perf job queued -> https://ci.internal/jobs/6421 (runs: nsys+perfetto on 4xA100 with env variants: NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE=PARALLEL | NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS | KV_CACHE_MAX_ITEMS=1e9) :white_check_mark:

maria: Thanks all — I'll run the two experiments now (bucketing-first + KV disable; then NCCL tuning + nsight capture) and paste the shorter perfetto snippets here. If anyone is around in 30m ping me and I can share the NSIGHT capture live. :thumbsup:

maria: one more note — in the nsys timeline I saw repeated small cudaMemsetAsync calls right before fused_attention_long kernels. Not sure if that's zero-fill for new KV pages or a memset from our allocator. Will instrument allocator to log memset vs free.

dan: good call. Memset implies host pinned pages being zeroed — that can serialize on the host. If allocator uses `cudaHostAlloc` + memset on host, that will show as CPU work in perfetto and block the loop. Try `cudaMemsetAsync` on device memory instead if possible.

maria: will try. will update thread with results.
